hints: Focus on what each observation tells you separately, temperature tells you about heat change and pressure tells you about gas moles.
Since heating lowers the yield of Z, the forward reaction must give out heat, so $\Delta H$ is negative.
Since lowering pressure also lowers the yield of Z, the forward reaction must make fewer moles of gas, so count gas molecules on each side to finish the match.
walkthrough:
**Use temperature to find the sign of ΔH**

Think of heat as a reactant or product. If raising temperature lowers the yield of Z, equilibrium has shifted backwards, away from Z.

By Le Chatelier, increasing temperature favours the endothermic direction. So the backward reaction must be endothermic, which means the forward reaction is exothermic.

$$\text{forward } \Delta H < 0$$

**Use pressure to compare gas moles**

Remember, only gas moles count for pressure effects. Lowering pressure shifts equilibrium to the side with more moles of gas.

Here lowering pressure lowers the yield of Z, so equilibrium shifts backwards. That means the backward side has more gas moles, and the forward side to make Z has fewer gas moles.

$$\text{moles of gas: reactants} > \text{moles of gas: products}$$

**Test the equations**

First keep only exothermic forward reactions. That leaves the two with $\Delta H = -100 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

Now check gas moles. $\text{X(g) + Y(g)} \rightleftharpoons \text{Z(g)}$ goes from 2 moles of gas to 1 mole of gas. This fits perfectly, fewer gas moles to make Z, so low pressure disfavours Z.

options.A: Forward reaction is exothermic ($\Delta H = -100 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$) so higher temperature shifts equilibrium left and lowers Z yield. Gas moles fall from 2 to 1, so lower pressure shifts equilibrium left and also lowers Z yield. Both observations match.
options.B: Gas moles are correct (2 to 1) but $\Delta H$ is wrong. With $\Delta H = +100 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ the forward reaction is endothermic, so higher temperature would increase the yield of Z, not lower it.
options.C: $\Delta H$ is correct (exothermic) but gas moles are backwards. Here $\text{X(s) + Y(g)} \rightleftharpoons \text{2Z(g)}$ goes from 1 mole of gas to 2 moles of gas. Lower pressure would favour Z and increase its yield, opposite to what is observed. Remember solids do not count.
options.D: Both effects are backwards. Endothermic forward means higher temperature would increase Z, and 1 to 2 gas moles means lower pressure would increase Z. This is the opposite of both given observations.
